2  ORDER Heard Sri B.Anwar Basha, learned counsel for the petitioners and Sri Praveena Y.Devareddiyavara,
learned HCGP for the respondent - State.

2. The petitioners are the accused Nos.2, 3 and 4 in Crime No.118/2023 of Women Police Station,
Ballari, seeking anticipatory bail for the offences punishable under Sections 498-A, 306 r/w 34 of Indian Penal Code (for short 'IPC').
3. Brief facts of the case:
It is the case of the prosecution that the father of the deceased has lodged a complaint stating that he has performed the marriage of his second daughter with the petitioner herein on 27.04.2019.
The couple had a child by name Girish.
The deceased was taken care nicely by the husband and in laws for eight months.
Thereafter, they started ill-treating and harassing her in one or the other pretext stating that she does not know the household work, cooking etc., and instigated her to commit suicide.

It is stated in the complaint that when the complainant went to the house of the deceased to see the grandson, the accused No.1 scolded the deceased in front of CW1 and did not allow the complainant/CW-1 to see his child.
4. On 19.07.2023, the CW1 has received a message from the relative of accused No.1 that, the deceased has committed suicide by hanging herself.
Hence, the complaint came to be registered against the petitioner and others.
The jurisdictional police have registered a case and conducted the investigation and submitted the charge sheet.

5. It is the submission of the learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner is innocent of the alleged offences, there were some petty issues and quarrels which were being taken place in the family as a matter of routine.
Both the petitioner and the deceased were living happily and also they have begotten a male child.

It is further submitted that the complainant has stated in his complaint that he was unnecessarily interfering with the affairs of the family of accused No.1 and there was a rift between CW1 and also the petitioner.
Accused No.1 was not allowing CW1 to go to see his grandson.
Taking advantage of the death of the deceased, the complainant has lodged a false complaint and implicated all the family members of the petitioner herein along with the petitioner.
There were no allegations against the petitioner and others in respect of the quarrel and cruelty prior to the suicide.
7. It is further submitted that there are no grounds to make out a case in respect of abatement to commit suicide.
There were no cases registered nor any panchayaths held in respect of cruelty or harassment.
The complainant intentionally filed a false complaint.

sentences.text: The petitioner is the permanent resident of Ward No.31, Karimaramma Colony, Ballari and was working as a coolie and he has to take care of his child NC: 2023:KHC-D:13471 and also the aged parents.
He will abide the conditions imposed by this Court in the event of his release on bail.
Making such submission, the learned counsel for the petitioner prays to allow the petition.

9. Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader submitted that the petitioner being the husband of the deceased always used to taunt and harass her on one or the other pretext and it is also established that she had committed suicide on account of cruelty said to have been committed by the petitioner.
The investigation is completed and charge sheet is filed.
At this stage, if the petitioner is enlarged on bail, there may be chances of absconding or fleeing away from justice.
Therefore, the petitioner is not entitled for bail.
Making such submission, the learned High Court Government Pleader prays to dismiss the petition.

10. Having heard the learned counsel for the respective parties and also perused the averments of the charge sheet, it appears that the petitioners are the NC: 2023:KHC-D:13471 in-laws of the deceased.
The entire allegations made against the accused No.1 in respect of insult that has been subjected to CW1, when CW1 had been to the house of the deceased to see his grandson.
The allegations against the petitioners are that they were staying along with the deceased in the house and they were harassing the deceased in one or the other pretext.
All the allegations are omnibus in nature and no specific overt-act has been attributed either in the complaint or in the charge-sheet.
11. The investigation is completed and the charge sheet is submitted.

The petitioners are women and aged about 51 years, 36 years and 38 years respectively and if the suitable conditions are imposed,
the apprehension of the prosecution would be met.

Hence, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed.

The petitioners are ordered to be enlarged on bail in Crime No.118/2023 of Women Police Station, Ballari, for NC: 2023:KHC-D:13471 the offences punishable under Sections 498-A, 306 r/w 34 of IPC, in the event of their arrest, on executing a personal bond in a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One lakh only) with one surety for the likesum to the satisfaction of the jurisdictional police and also the Trial Court,
subject to the following conditions:-
a) The petitioners shall appear before the Trial Court within one month from today and execute the personal bond and also furnish the surety.
b) The petitioners shall co-operate with the investigation.
c) The petitioners shall not tamper the prosecution witnesses nor hamper the proceedings of the Court.
